## Standard

<a id="GitHubRepositoryApi"></a>

### GitHub's API for a repository

`GitHubRepositoryApi` · `src/repository.ts:158`

The calls and the words that set a repository: its merge methods, automatic merges and merged branches deleted, its rulesets (a branch, the rules that protect it: no deletion, no rewriting, a pull request, the status checks required), the rules in force on a branch, its pages built by a workflow; and GitHub's command line, which makes the calls with the token of whoever runs it.

Source: GitHub REST API: Repositories (Get, Update a repository), Rules (Get rules for a branch; Get, Create and Update a repository ruleset), Pages (Get, Create a GitHub Pages site, build_type workflow); GitHub CLI manual: gh api (--method, --input) · `https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules`

## Vocabularies

<a id="MergeMethods"></a>

### How GitHub merges a pull request

`MergeMethods` · `src/repository.ts:27`

A merge commit keeps each commit of the branch (a generation is a commit); squashed, the branch is one commit; rebased, its commits are replayed on the main branch.

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `merge` | A merge commit: each commit of the branch kept |
| `squash` | One commit for the branch |
| `rebase` | Each commit replayed on the main branch |

## Architecture decision

<a id="RepositoryThroughItsApi"></a>

### A repository is set by its project's graph

`RepositoryThroughItsApi` · `src/repository.ts:276` · status: **held**

The settings of a repository are a decision of the project's graph, applied through a port of the library and read back: realized once for a machine (GitHub's command line) and once in memory.

Context: A repository's settings decide what reaches its main branch: set by hand in GitHub's pages, nothing says why, and nothing tells when they drift from what the project decided.

Consequences: A project decides its settings (RepositorySettings) and applies them by a program of its SDLC that a shipment deploys, which reads them back and compares them (RepositoryCompared); its scenarios play that program with the repository kept in memory, and a check reads the repository as it is.

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| A script the graph writes, which an administrator runs | nothing reads the repository back, and nothing records who set it |
| A writer in ci | a program that calls GitHub is code a project runs and verifies, not a file a place runs |

- Decided by: trame
- Serves: [Ports of the platform, realized once](product.md#RealizedOnce)
- Applied by: [How GitHub merges a pull request](#MergeMethods), [The parts of a repository's settings](#RepositoryParts), [A repository compared with its settings](#RepositoryCompared), [A repository on GitHub](#RepositoryApi), [GitHub's command line](#GitHubCliRepository), [The repositories a scenario keeps](#RepositoryKept), [A repository kept in memory](#RepositoryInMemory)

## Implementation

<a id="GitHubCliRepository"></a>

### GitHub's command line

`GitHubCliRepository` · `src/repository.ts:221`

Applies the settings by gh api, with the token of whoever runs it: the merge methods, the automatic merge and the deletion of merged branches; the ruleset named after the branch, created or replaced, whose rule of pull requests asks nothing but the approvals decided (GitHub's defaults otherwise); the pages built by a workflow, created or replaced. Reads back the repository, the rules in force on the branch, and its pages when asked. A call that fails stops what applies, and is answered.
